# Requests that Kunato must stop before they reach the upstream.
#
# One request per line:
#   METHOD TARGET [key=value ...]
#   - `ua`     sets the User-Agent header
#   - `body`   sets the request body
#   - `bodyhex` sets the request body from even-length hex bytes
#   - `body_file` reads the request body from a file relative to this list
#   - `chunked=1` sends the body with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (HTTP/1.1)
#   - `header` sets an arbitrary header using `Name: value`
#   - `proto=h2c` sends the request over HTTP/2 cleartext with prior knowledge
#   - `hpack_bomb=N` adds an HPACK compression bomb expanding to N extra fields
#     (requires `proto=h2c`)
#   - `pad_header=N` adds an `x-pad` header with N bytes of padding
#   - any other key becomes a request header
#   - values with spaces or quotes are quoted with "..."; use \" for a literal
#     quote and \\ for a backslash inside a quoted value
# Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored.
#
# These requests exercise the rules in rules.example.yaml. Run Kunato with a
# configuration that does not list this client in `trusted-sources`.

# --- SQL injection: blind inference and exfiltration channels ---
# `', (SELECT sleep(3))#` closes the INSERT string literal, evaluates the
# predicate in a subquery and comments out the tail. The same walkthrough
# infers one character or bit at a time (time and boolean channels) and reads
# values through the display (subquery, UNION) and error channels. Comments
# between a function name and its parenthesis must not hide the timing
# primitives.

POST /entries header="Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" body="name=%27%2C+%28SELECT+sleep%283%29%29%23"

GET /?id=1%20AND%20BENCHMARK/**/(5000000,1)
GET /?id=1%20WAITFOR%2F**%2FDELAY%20'0:0:3'
POST /entries header="Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" body="name=', (SELECT IF(SUBSTR((SELECT password FROM users LIMIT 1),1,1)='A',sleep(5),0))#"
POST /entries header="Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" body="name=', (SELECT IF(ASCII(SUBSTR((SELECT password FROM users LIMIT 1),1,1))&1=1,sleep(5),0))#"
GET /?id=1%27%20AND%20ASCII(SUBSTR(password,1,1))%3E64%23

# --- CVE-2021-41773 (Apache HTTP Server 2.4.49): encoded path traversal and CGI RCE ---

# spellings and must not bypass the filename rules.

# --- Upload content inspection: bytes that contradict the declared type ---
# A safe declared type (image, PDF, media, office, font) must not carry an
# executable, server-side script, or HTML payload. The engine rejects these
# before rule evaluation, so no filename rule is involved.
POST /upload header="Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=X" body_file=payloads/upload-php-in-jpeg.bin
POST /upload header="Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=X" body_file=payloads/upload-html-in-pdf.bin
POST /upload header="Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=X" body_file=payloads/upload-elf-in-png.bin
POST /upload header="Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=X" body_file=payloads/upload-gif-php.bin
# A safe claim must start with the claimed format's signature, so source code
# renamed to an image or PDF is rejected even without a script marker.
POST /upload header="Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=X" body_file=payloads/upload-ruby-in-jpeg.bin
POST /upload header="Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=X" body_file=payloads/upload-ruby-in-pdf.bin
# The example configuration enables `upload_inspection: strict`, so executable
# bytes behind a generic declared type are rejected as well.
POST /upload header="Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=X" body_file=payloads/upload-generic-elf.bin
# The script marker is beyond the first 1 KiB, after a valid GIF header and
# padding; the full-part scan must still reject it.
POST /upload header="Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=X" body_file=payloads/upload-gif-php-deep.bin
# PHP short tags are detected when the tag body looks like code, so a JPEG
# header followed by `<? system(...)` is rejected too, including a comment
# between the tag and the call.
POST /upload header="Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=X" body_file=payloads/upload-short-tag-in-jpeg.bin
POST /upload header="Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=X" body_file=payloads/upload-short-tag-comment-in-jpeg.bin
# A raw body sent to an executable or script path is scanned without a
# multipart envelope.
PUT /upload/polyglot.php header="Content-Type: application/x-httpd-php" body="<?php system($_GET[cmd]);?>"

# --- CVE-2026-34827 / CVE-2026-34829 (Rack): multipart parser denial of
#     service. 34827: escape-heavy quoted name/filename parameters drive
#     super-linear work in the part header parser. 34829: a chunked multipart
#     upload without Content-Length parses until EOF with no size bound. ---
POST /upload header="Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=X" body_file=payloads/multipart-escape-flood.txt
POST /upload header="Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=X" chunked=1 body_file=payloads/multipart-benign.txt

# --- Multipart boundary parser differentials (CVE-2026-26961 class): when a
#     Content-Type declares several boundaries, every interpretation must be
#     inspected. Rack parses the last boundary, so a payload visible only to
#     that boundary must not slip past the decoded-form rules. ---
POST /upload header="Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=safe; boundary=malicious" body_file=payloads/multipart-boundary-differential.txt

#     section. ---

# --- JWT attack classes left out ---
# Algorithm confusion (an RS256 token accepted after re-signing the public key
#   as an HMAC secret) and claim tampering have no static request shape;
#   signature and claim validation belong to the application.
# Weak-secret and default-secret re-signing is detectable only through known
#   public default tokens (CVE entries elsewhere in this file); arbitrary
#   forgery is not.
# Replay, expiry, and key-rotation abuse need server state, not a request
#   signature.
# JWE zip bombs and crit header abuse live inside the encrypted token and cannot
#   be inspected as a request.

# request line (binary Java serialization bodies, compressed ViewState payloads)
# are summarized at the end.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- 2025 attack classes left out ---
# CVE-2025-23006 (SonicWall) and CVE-2025-22457 (Ivanti): the public reports
#   describe proprietary or overflow payloads without a reproducible HTTP
#   request shape, so no probes are listed.
# CVE-2025-25257 (FortiWeb): the RCE step needs MySQL FILE privileges and a
#   follow-up request to the dropped webshell; the probes carry the header SQLi.
# CVE-2025-32432 (Craft CMS): execution needs a PHP payload planted in a log or
#   session file first; the probes carry the behavior-injection JSON.
# CVE-2025-47812 (Wing FTP): the injected Lua runs when a later request loads
#   the poisoned session; the probes carry the injection into /loginok.html.
# CVE-2025-58360 (GeoServer): exfiltration needs an attacker-controlled DTD or
#   a blind channel; the probes carry the XXE body.

# --- 2020 attack classes left out ---
# CVE-2020-1938 (Tomcat Ghostcat), CVE-2020-13934/13935 (Tomcat h2c upgrade
#   and WebSocket frame handling), CVE-2020-2551/2555/2883/14644 (WebLogic
#   T3/IIOP), CVE-2020-11651/11652 (Salt ZeroMQ): non-HTTP protocols or
#   connection-level framing; no request line can express them.
# CVE-2020-8193/8195/8196 (Citrix ADC/Gateway, KEV): the chain is
#   unauthenticated file read with public probes such as
#   /pcidss/report?type=allprofiles&... and /rapi/filedownload?filter=path:
#   but every CVE in the family scores below the 7.0 cut (6.5/6.5/4.3).
# CVE-2020-5405 (Spring Cloud Config, 6.5), CVE-2020-26258/26259 (XStream,
#   6.3/6.8): below the CVSS 7.0 cut and/or the payload is an XML body with a
#   converter class name, not a request-shaped attack.
# CVE-2020-11022/11023 (jQuery): client-side DOM handling; no server request
#   signature. CVE-2020-3580 (Cisco ASA, KEV): reflected client-side script.
# CVE-2020-17144 (Exchange EWS) and CVE-2020-1147/16952 (SharePoint) and
#   CVE-2020-0646 (.NET): the exploit is a serialized object inside a SOAP or
#   ViewState envelope; the only stable signature is the generic __VIEWSTATE
#   probe already listed for CVE-2020-0688.
# CVE-2020-2021 (PAN-OS SAML, KEV): exploitation needs a SAMLResponse whose
#   signature relationship to the IdP certificate is tampered, which is
#   indistinguishable from a legitimate POST to /SAML20/SP/ACS without IdP
#   trust material.
# CVE-2020-12271 / CVE-2020-15069 (Sophos XG Firewall) and CVE-2020-29574
#   (CyberoamOS): KEV-listed, but no public request shape was found in this
#   pass; exploitation details remain vendor-side.
# CVE-2020-5135 (SonicOS), CVE-2020-3259 / CVE-2020-3161 (Cisco ASA and IP
#   Phones), CVE-2020-8599 / CVE-2020-8467 (Trend Micro), CVE-2020-13671
#   (Drupal), CVE-2020-4006 (VMware), CVE-2020-15888 (Lua): memory-corruption
#   or configuration-injection bugs without a reproducible request shape, or
#   local/library flaws.
# CVE-2020-24363 (TP-Link TL-WA855RE): adjacent network (AV:A) factory reset.
# CVE-2020-35489 (Contact Form 7): the bypass uses characters in the uploaded
#   filename that depend on the form configuration; the probe carries the CF7
#   feedback endpoint with a .php filename.

# --- 2021 attack classes left out ---
# CVE-2021-26085 / CVE-2021-26086 (Confluence/Jira file read): KEV-listed but
#   CVSS 5.3, below the 7.0 selection threshold.
# CVE-2021-34429 (Jetty ambiguous URI): CVSS 5.3.
# CVE-2021-22214 (GitLab CI lint SSRF): CVSS 6.8, below the threshold.
# CVE-2021-33037 (Tomcat Transfer-Encoding parsing): CVSS 5.3; the generic
#   chunked-smuggling probes already cover the header shape.
# CVE-2021-36749 (Druid file read): CVSS 6.5; the sampler family is covered
#   by CVE-2021-25646.
# CVE-2021-45105 (Log4j2 DoS, 5.9) and CVE-2021-44832 (6.6, JDBC appender
#   configuration): below the threshold or configuration-specific.
# CVE-2021-22893 (Pulse Connect Secure, KEV, 10.0): the exploited iHub
#   deserialization has no public request shape; CVE-2021-22894 is an
#   authenticated buffer overflow.
# CVE-2021-22900 (Pulse Connect Secure): authenticated administrator upload.
# CVE-2021-27764: missing HttpOnly/Secure cookie flags, no attack request.
# CVE-2021-30116 (Kaseya VSA, KEV): the REvil attack chain has no public
#   request shape.
# CVE-2021-31166 (Windows HTTP.sys): heap-layout exploit; no stable request.
# CVE-2021-35211 (SolarWinds Serv-U, KEV): SSH vector, not HTTP.
# CVE-2021-26919 (Apache Druid JDBC): needs an attacker-run MySQL server;
#   no static request line.
# CVE-2021-27103 (Accellion FTA SSRF): no public request line.
# CVE-2021-25329 (Tomcat session persistence), CVE-2021-24122 (NTFS network
#   shares) and CVE-2021-41079 (TLS packet handling): configuration-specific
#   or connection-level, no request line.
# CVE-2021-33193 (httpd mod_h2 request splitting), CVE-2021-36160
#   (mod_proxy_uwsgi overread), CVE-2021-31618 / CVE-2021-41524 /
#   CVE-2021-26690 / CVE-2021-26691 (httpd DoS): raw h2 method bytes,
#   uwsgi mappings, or crash-only shapes.
# CVE-2021-4102 and the other 2021 Chrome/WebKit bugs are client-side.
# CVE-2021-31207 is CVSS 6.6 but is included inside the ProxyShell family
#   because the KEV chain relies on it together with CVE-2021-34473/34523.

# --- 2022 attack classes left out ---
# CVE-2022-22720 / CVE-2022-36760 (httpd request smuggling): triggered by
#   connection-level framing around a discarded body or an AJP backend, so the
#   generic Transfer-Encoding / Content-Length probes above already cover the shape.
# CVE-2022-31813 (httpd X-Forwarded-* stripping): the effect is only observable
#   at a proxied backend that trusts the headers; there is no distinct request.
# CVE-2022-28614 / CVE-2022-28615 / CVE-2022-29404 / CVE-2022-30556 (httpd):
#   large-input and mod_lua memory bugs without a stable request signature.
# CVE-2022-42252 (Tomcat): request smuggling through
#   invalid headers/framing; covered by the generic smuggling probes.
# CVE-2022-34305 / CVE-2022-45143 (Tomcat XSS): CVSS 6.1 / response-shaped error
#   pages; below the 7.0 threshold or not request-triggered.
# CVE-2022-29885 / CVE-2022-23181 / CVE-2022-25762 (Tomcat): cluster protocol,
#   local TOCTOU, and WebSocket race; not plain HTTP requests.
# CVE-2022-24706 (CouchDB): RCE runs over the Erlang distribution port (epmd /
#   9100), not HTTP.
# CVE-2022-26133 (Bitbucket): SharedSecretClusterAuthenticator is abused over
#   the Hazelcast cluster protocol, not HTTP.
# CVE-2022-41352 (Zimbra cpio): the trigger is a TAR attachment processed by
#   amavis after email delivery; no HTTP request carries it.
# CVE-2022-27925 (Zimbra): the authenticated variant of the CVE-2022-37042
#   probes above.
# CVE-2022-31657 / CVE-2022-31658 / CVE-2022-31659 (VMware Workspace ONE):
#   URL injection needs a victim redirect, and the RCE variants require an admin
#   session.
# CVE-2022-22960 / CVE-2022-31660 / CVE-2022-31661 (VMware): local privilege
#   escalation, no network request.
# CVE-2022-24682 / CVE-2022-27926 (Zimbra XSS): CVSS 6.1, below the threshold.
# CVE-2022-3590 (WordPress pingback SSRF): CVSS 5.9, below the threshold.
# CVE-2022-33980 (Commons Configuration) and CVE-2022-1471 (SnakeYAML):
#   library-only flaws; the request shape depends on the host application.
# CVE-2022-2068 (OpenSSL c_rehash): local command execution, no HTTP request.
# CVE-2022-42475 (FortiOS SSL-VPN): heap overflow driven by a binary payload
#   whose shape depends on the appliance build.
# CVE-2022-45378 (Apache SOAP RPCRouterServlet): the advisory confirms the
#   unauthenticated servlet but no public request-level PoC was found.
# CVE-2022-31656 / CVE-2022-31662: only the single verified traversal request
#   from public templates is listed.
# CVE-2022-22947 / CVE-2022-22965 / CVE-2022-22972 / CVE-2022-47966: the full
#   exploit chain needs follow-up requests or a signed SAML assertion; the listed
#   probe carries the injected or bypassing request.
# CVE-2022-24086: RCE needs a Magento template callback that only fires on some
#   builds; the probes carry the injected template directive.

# request line (binary bodies, connection-level framing) are summarized at the end.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- 2023 attack classes left out ---
# CVE-2023-2868 (Barracuda ESG): the command injection arrives inside a .tar
#   email attachment processed by the appliance, not in an HTTP request.
# CVE-2023-20269 (Cisco ASA/FTD): CVSS 5.0 and the exploit is a VPN
#   connection-profile brute force, not a single HTTP request.
# CVE-2023-37580 (Zimbra): CVSS 6.1 XSS below the score threshold.
# CVE-2023-38041 (Ivanti Secure Access Client): local (AV:L) TOCTOU.
# CVE-2023-33157 (SharePoint): authenticated RCE with no public request shape.
# CVE-2023-46748 (F5 BIG-IP) and CVE-2023-35081 (Ivanti EPMM): authenticated
#   SQLi/file-write; no public single-request PoC found in this pass.
# CVE-2023-46589 / CVE-2023-45648 / CVE-2023-42795 / CVE-2023-34981 /
#   CVE-2023-41080 (Tomcat): the trailer smuggling needs a trailer header over
#   the 8 KiB default limit, and the others are below 7.0 or response-driven.
# CVE-2023-27522 (httpd mod_proxy_uwsgi): triggered by a malicious upstream
#   response, not by the client request.
# CVE-2023-44487 / CVE-2023-43622 / CVE-2023-45802 (HTTP/2): rapid reset and
#   mod_http2 DoS need connection-level frame control (RST_STREAM, stalled
#   window updates) that a request line cannot express.
# CVE-2023-46604 (ActiveMQ OpenWire), CVE-2023-37582 / CVE-2023-33246
#   (RocketMQ remoting), CVE-2023-25194 (Kafka SASL/JNDI): binary, non-HTTP
#   protocols.
# CVE-2023-32784 (KeePass): local process memory. CVE-2023-38545 (curl): the
#   vulnerability is in the client. CVE-2023-36884 (Office/Windows HTML) and
#   CVE-2023-23397 (Outlook): client-side or email-triggered.
# CVE-2023-27992 (Zyxel NAS326/540/542, KEV): pre-auth command injection, but
#   no public request-shape PoC was found in this pass.
# CVE-2023-24078 (FuguHub): authenticated RCE; the public repository ships a
#   report only, with no reproducible request.

# request line (binary bodies, connection-level framing) are summarized at the end.
